pr_title: Drivers: Flash: stm32: G0 dual bank handling, G0 error check and CFGBSY check fixes
pr_body:
This PRs fixes several issues in the stm32g0 flash driver and introduces the checking of the  CFGBSY bit in the wait_flash_idle routine for all series supporting it.
Furthermore the integration_platforms for the drivers/flash test case are modified, such that several stm32 boards are build in CI.

Regarding dual bank flash bank layout on STM32G0:
This has only been tested on the g0b1re 512KiB flash target.
I am not sure about the influence of the DUAL_BANK option on 256KiB targets.
Does anybody of the ST guys know which SoC has FLASH_SALES_TYPE_0?
This seems to be the only type for which the DUAL_BANK option seems to have an influence on the number of banks (FLASH_BANK_NB)

Closes #37389
pr_comments:
Thanks for the review.
One reason why they could have chosen to use the flash sales type could be that the behavior has changed between revisions, but the naming of this register does not  really affirm something like that.

Regarding the dual bank option byte:
I have not been able to observe any differences on G0B1RE, whether this was set or not.
Basic flash operations and mcuboot updates with two image slots work on both configurations.
The FLASH_BANK_NB macro always returns 2 for G0B1RE, so most likely it only returns 1 for 256kiB SoCs when additionally OB_DUAL_BANK_VALUE is 0.
Would it be fine if -ENOTSUP is only returned in case OB_DUAL_BANK_VALUE is 0 and additionally CONFIG_FLASH_SIZE==256?
I have done it so in the latest update.

I can imagine that the effect of dual bank option byte, could be seen on mass erase operation:
* in single bank, the whole flash would be erased
* in dualbank, only half of the flash is erased (FLASH_CR_MER1)

Then I agree with you that G0B1RE always return FLASH_BANK_NB  =2 whatever the option byte.
But this sounds to me like a bug (probably stm32 HAL bug), thus I submitted an internal issue. 
So I don't think it is good to return -ENOTSUP only for CONFIG_FLASH_SIZE==256
But let's wait for the expert feedback. I set DNM label while waiting.
I have these changes in my `hawkbit` testing and it has been working great so far, I can confirm that it fixed #37389

> But let's wait for the expert feedback. I set DNM label while waiting.

Internal ref 111811. No update.
Unfortunately, no news.  I reiterate the internal request.

ping @str4t0m @ABOSTM @erwango 

maybe we should just get this through if there's no update from ST's expert? Personally I'd rather have some potential bug than the flash driver doesn't work at all (> 256KiB) for G0B1RE.
@erwango @cfriedt is this PR eligible to be back ported to v2.7?

issue_context.title: nucleo_g0b1re: Swapping image in mcuboot results in hard fault and softbricks the device
comments:
@ycsin,
I suppose that problem comes with introduction of nucleo_g0b1re, and more generally with introduction of stm32g0b1/stm32g0c1/...:
those MCU have flash dualbank whereas stm32g0 series formerly support only single bank.
So current stm32g0 flash driver is currently supporting only single bank.
Driver needs to be updated to support dual bank.

> @ycsin,
> I suppose that problem comes with introduction of nucleo_g0b1re, and more generally with introduction of stm32g0b1/stm32g0c1/...:
> those MCU have flash dualbank whereas stm32g0 series formerly support only single bank.
> So current stm32g0 flash driver is currently supporting only single bank.
> Driver needs to be updated to support dual bank.

Yup I noticed this just now, but so far I only found that the wait idle function needs to be updated as the G0X variant only checked BSY1 while the dualbank variants have BSY1 & BSY2. Haven't read through the G0B1 reference manual though.
I got an updated flash driver from @str4t0m which solved this issue, it is indeed due to the driver not supporting dual-bank flash yet. Pending @str4t0m to do a PR.
